subject: physics
topic: Gravitational field and simple harmonic motion

kept.q: Which of the following best defines gravitational field intensity (gravitational field strength) at a point?
options: The force experienced per unit mass placed at that point
The force experienced per unit charge placed at that point
The energy stored per unit mass at that point
The force experienced per unit area at that point
kept.explanation: Gravitational field strength is defined as the gravitational force acting on a unit mass placed at a point in the field. It is measured in N/kg, which also equals m/s^2.
kept.pidgin: Gravitational field strength na the force wey dey act on one kilogram mass for that point. E dey measured for N/kg, wey be same as m/s^2.

kept.q: A boy's school bag has a mass of 60 kg (including books) and weighs W on the Earth's surface, where g = 10 m/s^2. If the bag is taken to a height above the Earth's surface where the gravitational field strength reduces to one-quarter of its surface value, what is the new weight of the bag?
kept.explanation: Weight on Earth's surface = mg = 60 x 10 = 600 N. At the height given, g becomes 10/4 = 2.5 m/s^2, so new weight = 60 x 2.5 = 150 N.
kept.pidgin: For surface, weight = mg = 60 x 10 = 600 N. For that height, g don reduce to 2.5 m/s^2, so new weight = 60 x 2.5 = 150 N.

kept.q: A simple pendulum has a length of 4 m. Taking g as pi^2 m/s^2, calculate the period of oscillation of the pendulum.
kept.explanation: T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g) = 2*pi*sqrt(4/pi^2) = 2*pi*(2/pi) = 4 s. The pi cancels neatly because g was given as pi^2 m/s^2.
kept.pidgin: T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g) = 2*pi*sqrt(4/pi^2) = 2*pi*(2/pi) = 4 s. The pi cancel well-well because dem give g as pi^2 m/s^2.

kept.q: In simple harmonic motion, what is meant by the 'amplitude' of the motion?
options: The maximum displacement of the oscillating body from its mean (rest) position
The time taken for one complete oscillation
The number of oscillations made per second
The distance between two successive points moving in phase
kept.explanation: Amplitude is the greatest distance the oscillating body moves away from its equilibrium (mean) position during simple harmonic motion.
kept.pidgin: Amplitude na the biggest distance wey the body waka comot from im resting position when e dey oscillate.

kept.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude 5 cm and angular frequency 2 rad/s. Using v = omega*sqrt(A^2 - x^2), calculate the speed of the particle when its displacement from the mean position is 3 cm.

A simple pendulum has a period T when swinging on the Earth's surface, where the gravitational field strength is 10 m/s^2. If the same pendulum (same length) is taken to a planet where the gravitational field strength is 2.5 m/s^2, what is the new period in terms of T?
kept.explanation: Since T is proportional to 1/sqrt(g), the ratio of new period to old period is sqrt(g_earth/g_planet) = sqrt(10/2.5) = sqrt(4) = 2. So the new period is 2T; a weaker gravitational field makes the pendulum swing more slowly.
kept.pidgin: T dey proportional to 1/sqrt(g), so new period divide old period give sqrt(10/2.5) = sqrt(4) = 2. So new period na 2T; weak gravity make the pendulum swing slow-slow.
